title: SuperTrend
summary: A trailing line set a multiple of average true range away from the bar midpoint, which flips sides when the close breaks through it.
description:
SuperTrend builds two bands around the midpoint of each bar, the average of its high and low. Each band sits **Multiplier** times the average true range away from the midpoint. The average true range is a Wilder average of true range started from zero and scaled up by the factor that zero start leaves out, so it answers from the first bar. On the first bar the previous close is read as zero, which makes that bar's range very wide.

The bands only tighten toward price. The upper band moves down when the new basic band is lower, and the lower band moves up when the new basic band is higher; either one resets to the basic band when the previous close broke through it. The trend turns up when the close rises above the upper band and down when it falls below the lower band.

In an uptrend the line shows the lower band in green; in a downtrend it shows the upper band in red. A BUY label marks each turn up and a SELL label each turn down, and the first bar always carries one.
howToRead:
Green means the close has been holding above a trailing support, red that it has been holding below a trailing resistance. The line is often used as a trailing stop: it follows price in the direction of the trend and never moves against it until it flips. A BUY or SELL label marks the bar where the close crossed the line and the side changed.

In a sideways market the line flips often and each flip comes after the move, so the labels lag. A larger multiplier gives fewer and later flips, a smaller one more and earlier flips. The first stretch of bars is shaped by the very wide first range, so read the line once it has settled.

settings.label: ATR Period
settings.description: The length of the average true range that sizes the bands. A longer period gives steadier bands.

settings.label: Multiplier
settings.description: How many average true ranges the bands sit from the bar midpoint. A larger value means fewer, later flips.

settings.label: Source
settings.description: Kept as a setting, but the bands are built from the high, low and close whatever it is set to.

faq.q: Why is there a BUY label on the first bar?
faq.a: The trend starts as up, and the direction on the first bar is compared with no previous direction, so it always counts as a change.

faq.q: Why does the Source setting change nothing?
faq.a: The calculation uses the bar's high, low and close directly. The setting is kept so the study's settings match its usual layout, but it is not read.

faq.q: Can the line move against the trend?
faq.a: No. While the trend holds, the support line can only rise and the resistance line can only fall. It only jumps when the trend flips or when the previous close broke through the band.
